page: Microsoft Azure D64alds_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Daldv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 3780 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. The processor architecture is x86_64, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64alds_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving a top-tier rating in Geekbench multi-core performance and strong ratings in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests. Single-core performance is also strong, supported by high clock speeds and a robust L3 cache of 32 MB. Memory performance is characterized by strong write bandwidth for large blocks and strong read bandwidth for small cached blocks, though large-block read bandwidth remains average. The instance excels in parallelized workloads, as evidenced by strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation scores. It also shows strong performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput.

The D64alds_v6 offers high compute density and substantial local NVMe storage, making it highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring rapid local I/O and intensive CPU processing without massive memory footprints. However, the 2.0 GB of RAM per core represents a tradeoff for memory-bound applications, which may find the memory capacity restrictive. The instance is well-suited for high-throughput web serving, software compilation, database operations, and multi-threaded data processing tasks. It also supports moderate LLM inference workloads, showing strong text generation speeds for small and medium models, though prompt processing for larger models is average.
